entities.summary:
Lucius Cincius Alimentus was a celebrated Roman annalist, jurist, and provincial official from around 90 BCE to 30 BCE. He is principally remembered as one of the founders of Roman historiography, a field that aimed to create a coherent and systematic understanding of the Roman Republic's history. Alimentus's Annals, a comprehensive history of Rome from its mythical origins to the reign of Augustus, was a groundbreaking work that influenced the development of Roman historiography for centuries to come.


    Alimentus's work was heavily influenced by the Greek historian Polybius and the Roman historian Livy, and he is believed to have been a key figure in the development of the Roman historiographical tradition. His Annals covered the period from the founding of Rome in 753 BCE to the reign of Augustus, providing a detailed account of the Roman Republic's history, politics, and society.


    Alimentus's legacy extends beyond his own work, as his approach to historiography influenced later Roman historians such as Tacitus and Suetonius. His focus on the role of the Roman people in shaping their history also helped to establish the concept of 'Romanitas,' or Roman identity, which remained an important theme in Roman historiography for centuries.


    Despite the significance of his work, Alimentus's Annals have been lost, and only fragments remain in other works. Nevertheless, his contributions to Roman historiography and his impact on the development of the field remain an important part of the history of Western historiography.
